title: The Cost of Convenience
sentences: Almost everything I use now arrives without requiring any real effort on my part.
Food, films and conversation are all available within a single tap of a glass screen.
It took me several years to notice what that convenience had quietly taken away.
Waiting used to create small pockets of time in which nothing at all was demanded.
Those pockets have been filled in one by one, always by something more entertaining.
I am no longer convinced that the exchange has been made in my own favour.
The obvious objection to this complaint is reasonable enough, and I do accept it.
Nobody genuinely misses standing in a long queue at a bank on a Friday afternoon.
But convenience is rarely offered to us as a choice between two equal options.
It arrives already installed, and the alternative has to be rebuilt deliberately.
